title: The Crusades
summary: Armed pilgrimages from Western Europe to reclaim the Holy Land — from Urban II's call at Clermont to the kingdoms that briefly held Jerusalem.

stories.title: The First Crusade
stories.summary: From Pope Urban's summons to the storming of Jerusalem and the battle that followed.

events.title: Council of Clermont
events.body: Pope Urban II addressed a church council and nobles at Clermont, urging Western knights to aid the Byzantine Empire and recover Jerusalem from Muslim rule. His sermon ignited a wave of popular enthusiasm that would send tens of thousands eastward.

events.title: Siege of Nicaea
events.body: The crusader host laid siege to Nicaea, the Seljuk capital in Anatolia and a key obstacle on the road to Jerusalem. After weeks of assault the city surrendered to Byzantine forces, who had secretly negotiated its handover before the crusaders could sack it.

events.title: Battle of Antioch
events.body: After an eight-month siege, crusaders seized Antioch only to be immediately besieged in turn by a relieving Seljuk army. A desperate sortie led by Bohemond of Taranto routed the besiegers and secured the greatest city of northern Syria for the expedition.

events.title: Siege of Jerusalem 1099
events.body: A remnant of the original crusader army, now shrunken and starving, assaulted Jerusalem's walls in the summer heat. After fierce fighting the city fell on 15 July; the ensuing massacre of its inhabitants shocked even contemporaries.

events.title: Battle of Ascalon
events.body: An Egyptian Fatimid army marched north to retake Jerusalem while most crusaders were dispersing homeward. Godfrey of Bouillon led a surprise attack at Ascalon that shattered the Fatimid force and secured the newborn Kingdom of Jerusalem — for a time.

stories.title: Third Crusade
stories.summary: Richard the Lionheart, Saladin, and the fight for the coast.
